h.strategy: Aim for hypotheses you believe are about 60-75% likely to hold but that a careful expert would call uncertain: conditional effects rather than main effects. Good sources are diminishing returns (an improving edit helps less when the parent already has a similar strong component), damage concentration (a harmful edit hurts more when the parent has few alternative routes or little spare capacity), and asymmetry (adding a capability and removing it need not have mirror-image effects). Each hypothesis should name the mechanism in one sentence. Avoid claims that are merely definitional or true by construction, and avoid claims that need an unusual sign reversal to be true.

hyps.why: A strong conv path through node 2 already supplies capacity, so the direct 3x3 conv adds less.
Diminishing returns when the output already receives a strong direct conv input.
With edge 0 removed, node 1 is empty so a conv on edge 4 has nothing to process.
A strong conv from node 1 to the output lets the new conv on edge 0 contribute.
Removing the direct edge hurts more when there are few alternative routes to the output.
Damage concentrates when the other direct route to the output is already absent.
A skip filling an empty edge is a gain, while a skip replacing an existing conv is a downgrade.
With edge 0 removed, edge 2 gets no input from node 1, so the edit has almost no effect.
Edge 1 reaches the output only via edge 5, so with edge 5 removed the edit is inert.
Replacing a removed edge is a large gain, while replacing an existing stronger op gains little or loses accuracy.
